text.p: Singapore Refining Co (SRC) has cut output by an average of 40,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) for the period January 23 until February 3, a company source said on Monday.
"It already started cutting Thursday, to cut a total of 500,000 barrels," the source said.
A source had told Reuters last week that the 285,000-bpd refinery planned to cut its runs by 10-15,000-bpd for 10-15 days due to a delay in a crude cargo delivery.
The ship is now due to arrive on February 3 in the afternoon, when the cut in throughputs will be reviewed.
Two other refiners in Singapore have cuts runs by a total of 90,000-bpd this month due to refining losses.
General refining margins in Singapore have swung back into the black to around $1.00 per barrel as plunging product prices have found a floor, sources said.
"But all refineries are different and they are still negative for SRC whose breakeven costs are around $1.50," a source said.
